entryPoints.summary: The extension is structured around VS Code's contribution points, with specific features isolated in the `features/` directory.

entryPoints.description: The primary entry point where VS Code activates the extension and registers all commands and providers.
Centralized client for communicating with the Bob/Watsonx AI services.

layers.name: Integration Layer
layers.description: VS Code specific code including extension activation and command registration.

layers.name: Feature Layer
layers.description: Business logic for specific onboarding tools like Repo X-Ray and Day-N Plan.

dependencyGraph.dependencyFlow: VS Code -> Features -> Bob Client -> External API

artifacts.architectureDiagram:
graph TD
  Ext[extension.ts] --> Features
  Features --> Bob[bob/client.ts]
  Features --> Utils[utils/]
  Bob --> API[External AI API]
artifacts.criticalPathNarrative: When a command like 'X-Ray Repository' is triggered, the extension gathers workspace context (file tree, key files), passes it to the Bob Client which constructs a prompt, validates the JSON response using Zod, and finally renders a Markdown report.

conventions.rule: Use Zod schemas for all AI responses.
Use withProgress for any operation exceeding 1 second.

weirdParts.summary: A few utility scripts and manual implementations deviate from standard practices.

weirdParts.description: Utility scripts located in the root of the extension folder rather than a scripts/ directory.
weirdParts.hypothesis: Likely temporary or demo-specific automation for repo state management.
